claims.text: The macrobiotic Ma-Pi 2 diet produced a significantly greater reduction in fasting blood glucose compared to the standard recommended control diet in patients with type 2 diabetes.
The Ma-Pi 2 diet produced a significantly greater reduction in post-prandial blood glucose compared to the control diet in patients with type 2 diabetes.
The Ma-Pi 2 diet resulted in a significantly greater reduction in HbA1c levels compared to the control diet.
The Ma-Pi 2 diet achieved a significantly greater reduction in insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) compared to the control diet.
The Ma-Pi 2 diet resulted in a significantly greater reduction in total cholesterol compared to the control diet.
The Ma-Pi 2 diet resulted in a significantly greater reduction in LDL cholesterol compared to the control diet.
The Ma-Pi 2 diet resulted in a significantly greater reduction in LDL/HDL cholesterol ratio compared to the control diet.
The Ma-Pi 2 diet achieved a significantly greater reduction in BMI compared to the control diet.
The Ma-Pi 2 diet achieved a significantly greater reduction in body weight compared to the control diet.
The control diet group showed a significantly greater reduction in triglyceride levels compared to the Ma-Pi 2 diet group.
Neither diet produced a statistically significant change in HDL cholesterol levels from baseline.
A significantly higher proportion of patients achieved the target fasting blood glucose level of <= 110 mg/dl in the Ma-Pi 2 diet group compared with the control group.
A significantly higher proportion of patients achieved the target post-prandial blood glucose level of <= 140 mg/dl in the Ma-Pi 2 diet group compared with the control group.
A significantly greater reduction in oral hypoglycemic drug therapy was achieved in the Ma-Pi 2 group compared to the control group.

evidence.description: Adjusted linear quantile regression showed a significantly greater reduction in fasting blood glucose in the Ma-Pi 2 group compared to controls (regression coefficient 6.82, 95% CI: 1.79 to 13.46).

Adjusted linear quantile regression showed a significantly greater reduction in post-prandial blood glucose in the Ma-Pi 2 group compared to controls (regression coefficient 11.48, 95% CI: 5.39 to 31.44).
HbA1c reduction was significantly higher in the Ma-Pi 2 group than in the control group (regression coefficient 3.46, 95% CI: 1.28 to 5.46; p = 0.002).
HOMA-IR reduction adjusted for covariates including wrist circumference was significantly higher in the Ma-Pi 2 group (regression coefficient 15.14, 95% CI: 3.65 to 37.51).
Total cholesterol reduction had a regression coefficient of 18.61 (95% CI: 11.52 to 22.63) favoring the Ma-Pi 2 diet (p < 0.001).
LDL cholesterol reduction had a regression coefficient of 26.40 (95% CI: 21.37 to 34.50) favoring the Ma-Pi 2 diet (p < 0.001).
LDL/HDL ratio reduction had a regression coefficient of 31.54 (95% CI: 20.63 to 36.52) favoring the Ma-Pi 2 diet (p < 0.001).
BMI reduction regression coefficient was 2.99 (95% CI: 2.42 to 3.59) in favor of the Ma-Pi 2 diet (p < 0.001).
Weight reduction regression coefficient was 3.04 (95% CI: 2.39 to 3.58) favoring the Ma-Pi 2 diet (p < 0.001).
Triglycerides percentage change regression coefficient was -11.04 (95% CI: -24.41 to -2.92), indicating greater reduction in the control diet group.
HDL cholesterol change regression coefficient was 4.82 with 95% CI: -5.69 to 10.22 (including zero) and Wilcoxon rank-sum p = 0.283.
100% (19/19) of patients in the Ma-Pi 2 group vs 45% (9/20) in the control group achieved FBG target levels <= 110 mg/dl (difference 55.00%, 95% CI: 33.20 to 76.80).
100% (11/11) of patients in the Ma-Pi 2 group vs 53.33% (8/15) in the control group achieved PPBG target levels <= 140 mg/dl (difference 46.67%, 95% CI: 21.42 to 71.91).
5 out of 7 patients on OAD therapy suspended medication in the Ma-Pi 2 group compared to 1 patient in the control group (p = 0.018).

methodologies.name: Randomized open-label 21-day residential trial (MADIAB)
methodologies.description: A 21-day randomized, controlled, open-label trial comparing the macrobiotic Ma-Pi 2 diet with a control diet based on standard dietary recommendations for type 2 diabetes in a supervised residential setting.
conditions: Isocaloric energy restriction (1900 kcal/day for males, 1700 kcal/day for females)

limitations.text: The intervention was of short duration (21 days), limiting assessment of long-term sustainability and outcomes.
The trial lacked participant and attending medical staff blinding due to distinct differences in diet ingredients, taste, and appearance.
The trial had a relatively small sample size (51 participants completed the trial and were analyzed).
Standard recommended diets for type 2 diabetes frequently suffer from low adherence in real-life practice.

future_work.text: Conduct longer-term follow-up studies to confirm the results and investigate patient acceptance, compliance, and cost in real-life practice.
Elucidate potential underlying mechanisms of the Ma-Pi 2 diet, including changes in systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota composition.
